name: Sign-in attempt blocked
description: Sent when a sign-in to the account was refused — repeated wrong passwords, a failed second factor, or a network we do not trust — and the account holder has to say whether it was them.

origin.note: Design: siren — bookended bands. A reversed oxblood alarm band carries the headline, a thick rule cuts it off, the attempt is tabled on white, and a sober charcoal band closes on the record.

subject: We blocked a sign-in to your {{ product.name }} account
preheader: The attempt did not succeed. We need to know whether it was yours.

user.first_name.description: Names the person so the alert reads as being about their account and not a broadcast. Omitted cleanly when unknown.

status_label.description: The severity word inside the alarm band. It is set beside a square mark so the state survives colour blindness, greyscale and forced inversion.

heading_text.description: The headline, reversed out of the alarm band. Keep it short — it is the only line most people read on a lock screen.
heading_text.default: We blocked a sign-in to your account

band_line.description: The one reassurance that has to arrive before anything else: this was an attempt, not a breach.
band_line.default: Nothing was accessed. The attempt was stopped before it reached your account.

body.description: Why the block happened, in the plainest terms available. Guessing is worse than admitting the trigger is mundane.
body.default: A sign-in was refused after several wrong passwords in a row. That usually means someone was guessing, and occasionally it means a saved password somewhere has gone stale.

attempt_label.description: Heading above the metadata table. A separate field because teams word this differently — "The attempt", "Request detail", "What we saw".

attempt.description: What was observed, as `label` / `value` pairs. Set `mono` on anything a person may have to read character by character, such as an IP address. Send only what you actually recorded; a row reading "Unknown" invites a support ticket.

location_caveat.description: Pre-empts the commonest reply to this email, which is "that isn't my city". IP geolocation is routinely wrong by a region.
location_caveat.default: Location is estimated from the network address and is often wrong by a city or more, particularly on mobile data or a VPN.

secure_url.description: The lock-down path: sign out every session and force a password change. This is the heavy action and carries the filled button.

secure_label.description: Label for the lock-down action. Write it in the first person so it reads as the reader's decision, not an instruction.

confirm_url.description: Optional acknowledgement that clears the block for that device. Offering it stops people locking themselves out over their own forgotten password.

confirm_label.description: Label for the light action. Deliberately outlined, never filled — it must not compete with locking down.

choice_note.description: What each button actually does. People hesitate over security buttons precisely because nobody tells them the consequence.
choice_note.default: Confirming clears the block for that device. Securing the account signs out every session everywhere and starts a password change.

record_note.description: The closing band. States that the message is a record rather than a demand, so ignoring it is a legitimate choice.
record_note.default: An automated security record. We send one for every blocked attempt, whether or not you act on it, so that a silent lockout can never happen.
